chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh narrated from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ishaq ibn Ammar al-Sayrafi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding the Fitrah (alms of fasting)? Is it permissible for me to pay it in silver at the value of these specific items that you have mentioned?' He said, 'Yes, indeed that is more beneficial for him.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr), the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.فِضَّة: Silver, used here as a form of currency/value

ai.seo_question: Can Fitrah be paid in money or silver instead of food?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the substitution of specific food items for their monetary equivalent (Qimah) in Fitrah, highlighting the principle of 'nafa'' (benefit/utility) in fulfilling religious obligations. This ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence to adapt fixed obligations to contemporary economic contexts, allowing the payer to maximize the charitable impact by purchasing what is most needed or beneficial. The emphasis on silver as the medium reflects the historical standard of value in early Islamic society, while the permission to choose the purchase item prioritizes the recipient's welfare over rigid formalism.
